title: 16,000 people played my AI-built game last month. I use the free browser version as a funnel to the monetized app.
author: MightyBig-Dev
selftext:
I’ve been casually building Nelly Jellies with Codex for about six months, a few hours each week. Six months ago, 174 people played it. Last month, more than 16,000 did.

My strategy is pretty simple. I only share the free browser version. People can click and play without downloading anything or creating an account. 

If they enjoy it, the native app has some extra bonuses and that’s where I monetize through rewarded ads and Jelly Pro. 

Has anyone else tried this funnel?  Do you have any questions?  I’m happy to help the community where I can.  
AI game dev is beyond fun. 

If you try it, drop your high score! 💜🐙

replies.author: HEXAPONG
replies.body:
Unfortunately, it appears your DMs are turned off. 

For the sake of convenience, I can post my questions here. 

First, the game is beautiful, fun and I enjoy the music. I've downloaded the app on my phone and I will be putting in my hours and plan on leaving a review. 

I think your approach is brilliant and I hope to pick your brain. 

1. What service are you using for your leaderboards? They appear cross platform from looking at them in the web browser and on the iOS app. 
2. How do you manage vulgar and other inappropriate names from being on the leaderboard?
3.  What has been your greatest challenge so far?
4. Do you plan on releasing Nelly Jellies on Steam?

replies.author: MightyBig-Dev
replies.body:
Sorry about that! I had no idea my DMs were turned off or how that happened, but they’re open now.

Thank you for the kind words, downloading the app, and planning to leave a review. I really appreciate it!!!

I use Firebase, specifically Cloud Firestore, for the leaderboards. The web, iOS, and Android versions all connect to the same database, which keeps the leaderboards cross-platform.

Display names go through an automated filter before they’re accepted. It blocks common profanity, some disguised spellings, reserved names, links, contact information, and unsupported characters. No filter is perfect, so I can expand it whenever something slips through.

The biggest challenge is managing the scope. Nelly Jellies is a hobby I work on for a few hours each week, so maintaining three platforms while continually adding jellies, powerups, events, and other content can be a lot to balance.

I haven’t ruled out Steam, but I don’t have any concrete plans for it yet. Right now I’m focused on improving the web and mobile versions, but I’d love to explore Steam eventually.  I’m working slowly on a desktop only game called [Rope Ninja](http://ninja.mightybig.ca) which I plan to release on steam in 2055 lmao. 

Hope this was all helpful.

replies.author: HEXAPONG
replies.body:
Brother, I appreciate the detailed reply! I think my total play time is about 2 hours now and I just left a review. 

I've been dabbling with my own project and like you said the scope is the biggest challenge. For me its been every step of the way from first building a browser based HTML game, to then repackaging it to iOS and now figuring out hosting, domain, leaderboards, signing in with Google/Apple. Don't get me wrong, I love the challenge. I just wish I had more time in the day haha.

The only thing I thought though is that I kept having to make myself keep playing after a little while. I got all the power ups, multiple times, cleared the board multiple times, etc. I eventually just stopped playing because I didn't really see much reason to continue, because I felt like I would literally go on all night. That may seem like a good thing to keep people playing, but there wasn't anything keeping me there after I realized how simple it was. The game is great overall though. Awesome job.
